content: Post-viral fatigue syndrome (PVFS) is a medical condition characterized by a state of persistent fatigue that arises following a viral infection. Although the term post-viral fatigue syndrome is not widely used, the phenomenon of experiencing prolonged or severe fatigue after recovering from an illness is relatively common. In some individuals, this fatigue and associated symptoms can persist for months or even years after a severe viral infection. In the World Health Organization's International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10), PVFS is categorized under other disorders of the brain, which is a neurological classification with the code G93.3. Importantly, PVFS is explicitly excluded from being classified as a neurotic disorder. Within this classification, Benign Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME) is listed under PVFS. Additionally, alternative diagnoses such as Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS) and Neuromyasthenia are included in the ICD-10's alphabetical index. Post-viral syndromes encompass a broader range of conditions, which may include post-polio syndrome, late-stage Lyme disease, and potentially chronic mononucleosis or other severe chronic viral infections. Some researchers propose that PVFS represents a biological state of immune system dysfunction, weakness, or damage. This immune system dysregulation is thought to be a common feature across various post-viral syndromes. It is anticipated that advancements in immune system research, particularly in the context of HIV, may provide valuable insights into the mechanisms underlying post-viral syndromes and pave the way for improved treatment options.
